item.content:encoded:
There is potential here, but it's drowned out by sub-par execution.

-1 and lobbying for a rewrite.

My headcanon is that the music is actually the animating force.
The residents of [French town] were all killed or driven away when the war swept over their little hamlet. But one stubborn old man refused to leave the place he'd grown up, the town where his wife was buried. So he arranged for a protector. Consulting tattered manuscripts long-dismissed in the catacombs of the local church; he repurposed the bombed out husk of a tank abandoned in the last offensive. The ritual called for a priest to recite holy chants as long as "the consecrated" was to remain animated. But our lone survivor wanted something more reliable than his old smoker's lungs. So instead he incorporated the phonograph that was his only respite from the damnable silence of his murdered home town. Improvising with ancient forbidden rites is not recommended, and now we have a "Magician's Apprentice" situation that has long outlived the caster; and will carry on protecting the town until that phonograph and worn-out record collection in the former engine compartment finally wear down to nothing.

Of course, The Foundation has no way of knowing any of that.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, this one could use a tone touchup. There are also some things unclear or otherwise out of place about it. Such as: Why is this not Keter? What's the deal with it playing music? Can it fire its weapons or not? If not, then why is it not more thoroughly contained? And if it can, shouldn't that be clearly noted in the article given how much more dangerous that makes it and given how the weapons are described as mechanically broken?

It's a -1 for me. A rewrite to fix the aforementioned stuff and to actually go somewhere with the "maybe it is/used to be guarding something" angle would make it a lot better, but as it stands the execution of the idea is lacking.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: While I enjoy the concept of this SCP it might benefit from a clarification on specific ways the tank attacks. This could be presented in a variety of ways such as an incident report or simply a testing log. "…will constantly attack and harass them in any way possible" really feels like it leaves too much to the imagination. It is established that it's guns are not operational so one would have to assume that it rams the subjects of attack and barring that perhaps the musical qualities of this SCP cause some kind of damage. If it is just the ramming then I would have to wonder what the trouble in keeping a centralised containment is.
